translations.literal: From now on the investigating censors should be ordered to tour by route and report good and ill alike.”
translations.idiomatic: From now on have investigating censors tour by route and report both good and ill.”

sentences.zh: 」上嘗命左衛將軍大磐訪求良弓，而磐多自取，護衛婁室以告，上命點檢司鞫磐。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered Left Guard General Dapan to seek out fine bows; Dapan took many for himself, and guard Lou Shi reported it—the emperor ordered the Inspection Office to try Dapan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had once ordered Left Guard General Dapan to find fine bows; Dapan kept many for himself, and guard Lou Shi reported it—the emperor ordered the Inspection Office to investigate Dapan.

sentences.zh: 磐妹為寶林，磐屬內侍僧兒言之寶林，寶林以聞，命杖僧兒百，出磐為隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: Dapan’s younger sister was Baolin; Dapan asked the inner attendant Seng’er to speak to Baolin, and Baolin reported it. The emperor ordered Seng’er flogged a hundred strokes and Dapan sent out as defense commissioner of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dapan’s younger sister was the consort Baolin; he had inner attendant Seng’er speak to her, and she reported it. The emperor ordered Seng’er flogged a hundred times and sent Dapan out as defense commissioner of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月己丑朔，以戒諭官吏貪墨，詔中外。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on jichou, the new moon, an admonition against official corruption was issued to the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jichou, the new moon, an edict warning officials against corruption was proclaimed within and without.

sentences.zh: 乙未，命涿州刺史兼提點山陵，每以朔望致祭，朔則用素，望則用肉，仍以明年正月為首。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Zhuo prefect was also made commissioner for the imperial tombs, to offer sacrifice at each new and full moon—plain offerings at the new moon and meat at the full moon—and the next year’s first month was made the starting point.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Zhuo prefect was also named commissioner for the imperial tombs, to sacrifice at every new and full moon—plain food at the new moon, meat at the full—and the first month of the coming year was set as the start.

sentences.zh: 及命圖畫功臣於太祖廟，其未立碑者立之。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to paint the meritorious ministers in Taizu’s temple and to erect steles for those who had none.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to paint the meritorious ministers in Taizu’s temple and erect steles where none yet stood.

sentences.zh: 以翰林待制靖為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: Hanlin attendant drafting officer Jing was made birthday envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin attendant drafting officer Jing was sent as birthday envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「海陵時，修起居注不任直臣，故所書多不實。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: “In Hailing’s time the Diary of Activity and Repose did not employ upright men, so what was written was largely untrue.
translations.idiomatic: He told the chief ministers: “Under Hailing the Diary of Activity and Repose did not use upright men, so most of what was written was false.

sentences.zh: 可訪求得實，詳而錄之。

translations.literal: You should seek out the truth and record it in detail.”
translations.idiomatic: Seek out the truth and record it in full.”

sentences.zh: 」參政孟浩進曰：「良史直筆，君舉必書，自古帝王不自觀史，意正在此。

translations.literal: Participation Councillor Meng Hao advanced and said: “A good historian’s straight brush—whatever the ruler does, he is sure to write; from antiquity emperors did not themselves read the diary, and the point was precisely this.”
translations.idiomatic: Participation Councillor Meng Hao said: “A good historian’s honest brush records whatever the ruler does; since antiquity emperors did not read the diary themselves—that was the whole point.”

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，詔罷複州歲貢鹿筋。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict abolished Fuzhou’s annual tribute of deer sinew.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ended Fuzhou’s annual tribute of deer sinew.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙丑，幸東宮。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on yichou, he visited the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yichou, he visited the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 以同簽大宗正事辟合土等為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: Co-signing grand clan steward Piheitu and others were made envoys to congratulate Song at New Year.
translations.idiomatic: Co-signing grand clan steward Piheitu and others were sent as New Year envoys to Song.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子朔，遣武定軍節度使移剌按等招諭阻珝。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on wuzi, the new moon, Wuding Army military commissioner Yelü An and others were sent to summon and instruct Zuxu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, the new moon, Wuding Army commissioner Yelü An and others were sent to summon and instruct Zuxu.

sentences.zh: 九年正月戊午朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Ninth year, first month, on wuwu, the new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, on wuwu, the first month’s new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent New Year envoys.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上與宣徽使敬嗣暉、秘書監移剌子敬論古今事，因曰：「亡遼日屠食羊三百，亦豈能盡用，徒傷生耳！

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor discussed past and present affairs with Palace Attendants Commissioner Jing Sihui and Secretariat Director Yelü Zijing, and said: “When Liao perished they slaughtered three hundred sheep a day—how could they possibly use them all? They only wasted life!
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he discussed past and present with Palace Attendants Commissioner Jing Sihui and Secretariat Director Yelü Zijing and said: “When Liao fell they butchered three hundred sheep a day—could they possibly use them all? They only destroyed life!

sentences.zh: 朕雖處至尊，每當食，常思貧民饑餒，猶在己也。

translations.literal: Though I stand in the utmost honor, whenever I eat I always think of the poor starving—as if it were myself.
translations.idiomatic: Though I stand supreme, whenever I eat I think of poor men hungry and cold—as if it were my own hunger.

sentences.zh: 彼身為惡而口祈福，何益之有？

translations.literal: Those who do evil in person yet pray with their mouths—what good can that do?”
translations.idiomatic: Men who do evil yet pray with their lips—what good is that?”

sentences.zh: 如海陵以張仲軻為諫議大夫，何以得聞忠言。

translations.literal: When Hailing made Zhang Zhongke remonstrance officer, how could he hear loyal words?
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing made Zhang Zhongke remonstrance officer, how could he hear honest counsel?

sentences.zh: 朕與大臣論議一事，非正不言，卿等不以正對，豈人臣之道也！

translations.literal: When I discuss a matter with you ministers, if it is not right I do not speak of it—yet you do not answer me straight. Is that the way of a minister!”
translations.idiomatic: When I take up a matter with you ministers, if it is not right I do not pursue it—yet you do not answer straight. Is that how ministers should act!”

sentences.zh: 」庚午，詔諸州縣和糴，毋得抑配百姓。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an edict ordered the prefectures and counties in tax-grain purchases not to force allocations on the people.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu an edict ordered prefectures and counties not to force allocations on the people in tax-grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，契丹外失剌等謀叛，伏誅。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Khitan Waila and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Khitan Waila and others plotted rebellion and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，制漢人、渤海兄弟之妻，服闋歸宗，以禮續婚者，聽。

translations.literal: On bingxu, a statute allowed Han Chinese and Bohai who, after a brother’s wife’s mourning was complete, returned to her natal clan and married her in due ritual to do so.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu a statute allowed Han and Bohai men who, after a brother’s wife had completed mourning and returned to her natal clan, to remarry her by proper rite.

sentences.zh: 二月庚寅，制妄言邊關兵馬者，徒二年。

translations.literal: Second month, on gengyin, whoever falsely spoke of border troops and horses was sentenced to two years’ penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengyin, false talk of border troops and horses was punished with two years’ penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔改葬漢二燕王於城東。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict ordered the two Yan kings of Han reburied east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen an edict ordered the two Han Yan kings reburied east of the city.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以中都等路水，免稅，詔中外。

translations.literal: On gengzi, because the Central Capital route and others had suffered flood, taxes were remitted and an edict was issued to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, because the Central Capital route and others had flooded, taxes were remitted and an edict proclaimed through the realm.

sentences.zh: 又以曹、單二州被水尤甚，給複一年。

translations.literal: Because Cao and Shan prefectures had suffered especially heavily from water, they were given a full year’s remission.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cao and Shan had suffered especially from the floods, they were given a full year’s remission.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔女直人與諸色人公事相關，只就女直理問。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict ordered that when Jurchens and people of other categories had official business with one another, inquiry was to be conducted only under Jurchen law.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin an edict ordered that when Jurchens and people of other categories had official dealings together, cases were to be tried only under Jurchen law.

sentences.zh: 三月丁巳朔，萬春節，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingsi, the new moon, Ten-Thousand Springs festival; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingsi, the new moon, the Ten-Thousand Springs festival; Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以尚書省定網捕走獸法，或至徒，上曰：「以禽獸之故而抵民以徒，是重禽獸而輕民命也，豈朕意哉！

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Secretariat fixed the law on netting and chasing game, with penalties up to penal servitude. The emperor said: “To punish the people with servitude because of birds and beasts is to value beasts and slight human lives—is that my intent?
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Secretariat set penalties for netting and chasing game, up to penal servitude. The emperor said: “To send people to servitude over birds and beasts is to value animals and slight human lives—is that my intent?

sentences.zh: 自今有犯，可杖而釋之。

translations.literal: From now on offenders may be flogged and released.”
translations.idiomatic: From now on offenders may be flogged and released.”

sentences.zh: 」詔御史中丞移剌道廉問山東、河南。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yelü Dao to conduct a circuit inspection of Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yelü Dao to inspect Shandong and Henan on circuit.

sentences.zh: 辛未，禁民間稱言「銷金」，條理內舊有者，改作「明金」字。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the people were forbidden to use the term “dissolving gold”; wherever it appeared in regulations it was changed to read “bright gold.”
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the people were forbidden to say “dissolving gold”; wherever the old term appeared in regulations it was changed to “bright gold.”

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以大名路諸猛安民戶艱食，遣使發倉廩減價出之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, because the meng’an households of Daming Route lacked food, envoys were sent to open the granaries and sell grain at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, because meng’an households in Daming Route lacked food, envoys were sent to open the granaries and sell grain at reduced prices.

sentences.zh: 四月己丑，謂宰臣曰：「朕觀在位之臣，初入仕時，競求聲譽以取爵位，亦既顯達，即徇默苟容為自安計，朕甚不取。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on jichou, he told the chief ministers: “I observe that when ministers first enter office they all strive for reputation to win rank; once they are eminent they fall silent and seek only their own ease—I will not have it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jichou, he told the chief ministers: “I see that when men first take office they scramble for reputation to win rank; once eminent they hold their tongues and seek only ease—I will not accept it.

sentences.zh: 宜宣諭百官，使知朕意。

translations.literal: You should proclaim this to the hundred offices so they know my mind.”
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this to the hundred offices so they know my mind.”

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，遣翰林修撰蒲察兀虎、監察御史完顏鶻沙分詣河北西路、大名、河南、山東等路勸猛安謀克農。

translations.literal: On guisi, Hanlin reviser Pucha Wuhu and investigating censor Wanyan Gusha were separately sent to Hebei West Route, Daming, Henan, Shandong, and other routes to urge the meng’an and mouke to farm.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Hanlin reviser Pucha Wuhu and investigating censor Wanyan Gusha were sent separately to Hebei West Route, Daming, Henan, Shandong, and other routes to urge meng’an and mouke to farm.

sentences.zh: 五月丙辰朔，以符寶郎徒單懷貞為橫賜高麗使，宿直將軍完顏賽也為橫賜夏國使。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingchen, the new moon, Seal and Treasures officer Tushan Huaizhen was made side-gift envoy to Goryeo and night-duty general Wanyan Saiye side-gift envoy to Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the new moon, Seal and Treasures officer Tushan Huaizhen was sent as side-gift envoy to Goryeo and night-duty general Wanyan Saiye as side-gift envoy to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，尚書省奏越王永中、隋王永功二府有所興造，發役夫。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Secretariat reported that the households of Prince Yongzhong of Yue and Prince Yonggong of Sui had undertaken construction and levied corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Secretariat reported that the households of Prince Yongzhong of Yue and Prince Yonggong of Sui had begun construction and levied corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕見宮中竹有枯瘁者，欲令更植，恐勞人而止。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “I saw withered bamboo in the palace and wished to have it replanted, but feared troubling the people and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “I saw withered bamboo in the palace and wished to have it replanted, but stopped for fear of troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 二王府各有引從人力，又奴婢甚多，何得更役百姓。

translations.literal: Each of the two princely households already has escort manpower, and there are many slaves and maids—how can they levy the common people again?
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two princely households already has escort manpower and many slaves and maids—why levy the common people again?

sentences.zh: 爾等但以例為請，海陵橫役無度，可盡為例耶！

translations.literal: You only cite precedent in your request—Hailing’s forced corvée knew no limit; can that all be taken as precedent!”
translations.idiomatic: You only cite precedent—Hailing’s forced corvée knew no limit; can that all be precedent!”

sentences.zh: 自今在都浮役，久為例者仍舊，於並官給傭直，重者奏聞。」

translations.literal: From now on, for floating corvée in the capital, where long-standing practice continues as before, hired wages are to be paid uniformly from government funds; heavy cases are to be memorialized.”
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for floating corvée in the capital, long-standing practice may continue, but hired wages are to be paid from government funds; heavy cases are to be memorialized.”

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅，冀州張和等反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on gengyin, Zhang He and others of Jizhou rebelled and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengyin, Zhang He and others rebelled in Jizhou and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以久旱，命宮中毋用扇。

translations.literal: On wuxu, because of prolonged drought, the palace was ordered not to use fans.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, because of prolonged drought, the palace was forbidden to use fans.

sentences.zh: 庚子，雨。

translations.literal: On gengzi, it rained.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi it rained.

sentences.zh: 七月乙卯朔，罷東北路采珠。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on yimao, the new moon, pearl collecting on the Northeast Route was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on yimao, the new moon, pearl collecting on the Northeast Route was abolished.

sentences.zh: 壬申，觀稼於近郊。

translations.literal: On renshen, he viewed the crops in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he viewed the crops in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 八月甲申朔，有司奏日食，以雨不見，伐鼓用幣如常禮。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiashen, the new moon, the offices reported a solar eclipse; because of rain it was not seen, and drums were beaten and silks used as in the regular rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiashen, the new moon, the offices reported a solar eclipse; rain hid it, and drums were beaten and silks offered as in the regular rites.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅朔，以刑部尚書高德基等為賀宋生日使，宿直將軍僕散守中為夏國生日使，提點司天臺馬貴中為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiayin, the new moon, Minister of Punishments Gao Deji and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the imperial birthday; night-duty general Pusan Shouzhong was made Western Xia birthday envoy; and Ma Guizhong, superintendent of the Directorate of Astronomy, was made Goryeo birthday envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin, the new moon, Minister of Punishments Gao Deji and others were sent to congratulate Song on the imperial birthday; night-duty general Pusan Shouzhong was sent as Western Xia birthday envoy; and Ma Guizhong, superintendent of the Directorate of Astronomy, as Goryeo birthday envoy.

sentences.zh: 罷皇太子月料，歲給錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: The crown prince’s monthly stipend was abolished; fifty thousand strings of cash were given yearly instead.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince’s monthly stipend was abolished; fifty thousand strings of cash were granted yearly instead.

sentences.zh: 上謂台臣曰：「比聞朝官內有攬中官物以規貸利者，汝何不言？

translations.literal: The emperor told the censorate officials: “I have lately heard that among court officials some seize inner-attendant goods to seek loan profit—why do you not speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the censorate: “I hear that some court officials seize inner-attendant goods to seek loan profit—why do you not report it?

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「不知。

translations.literal: ” All replied: “We did not know.”
translations.idiomatic: ” All replied, “We did not know.”

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕尚知之，汝有不知者乎？

translations.literal: ” The emperor said: “If even I know it, can there be things you do not know?
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor said: “If even I know it, can you not know?

sentences.zh: 朕若舉行，汝將安用！

translations.literal: If I were to act on it, what use would you be!”
translations.idiomatic: If I acted on it, what use would you be!”

sentences.zh: 」壬戌，秋獵。

translations.literal: ” On renxu, the autumn hunt.
translations.idiomatic: ” On renxu he held the autumn hunt.

sentences.zh: 十月丁亥，還都。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on dinghai, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on dinghai, he returned to the capital.

translations.idiomatic: On bingwu a grand offering was performed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以平章政事完顏思敬為樞密使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Associate Administration Councillor Wanyan Sijing was made privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Associate Administration Councillor Wanyan Sijing became privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月己未，以尚書左丞完顏守道為平章政事，右丞石琚為左丞，參知政事孟浩為右丞。

translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiwei, Left Vice Director Wanyan Shoudao became associate administration councillor; Right Vice Director Shi Ju became left vice director; and Participation Councillor Meng Hao right vice director.

translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.

translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Jingzhao intendant Yi and others were sent as envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.

translations.literal: On renxu, the winter hunt.

translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital regent Tushan Hexi became associate administration councillor.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Venus was seen in daylight.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，獵於近郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou, he hunted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he hunted in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 丙午，制職官犯公罪，在官已承伏者，雖去官猶論。

translations.idiomatic: On bingwu a statute was enacted: when officials commit public crimes and have already confessed in office, they are still prosecuted even after leaving office.

sentences.zh: 十年正月壬子朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, first month, on renzi, the new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent congratulatory envoys.

translations.literal: On jiazi, the palace was ordered not to hang lanterns at the Lantern Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the palace was forbidden to hang lanterns at the Lantern Festival.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以司徒、御史大夫李石為太尉、尚書令。

translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief Li Shi was made grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat.

translations.idiomatic: On wushen he told his close ministers: “After the guard escort corps, all will be officials who govern the people—have them taught to read.”

translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he told Participation Councillor Zong Xu: “When you were Henan army commander you spoke of the advantages and harms of Yellow River dikes and embankments, which accorded very well with my mind.

translations.idiomatic: I constantly think of the people’s tax and corvée levies, how officials cheat one another, fail to plan early, and at the deadline levy in desperate haste—the cost doubles and more, and the harm is great.

translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yimao, he went to the Liuhe River valley.

translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengchen, Ren Dejing of Western Xia coerced his lord Li Renxiao into memorializing the throne to request that the state be divided in two.

translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on renwu, the autumn hunt.

translations.idiomatic: On wuxu corvée men working the hunting enclosure were released.

sentences.zh: 詔扈從糧食並從官給。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that food for the entourage be supplied by the accompanying officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the entourage’s provisions be supplied by the accompanying officials.

translations.idiomatic: On yisi an order directed that entourage members who let livestock graze and trample crops were to be flogged and still pay compensation.

translations.idiomatic: On renshen Participation Councillor Zong Xu was sent on a northern inspection tour.

translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengchen, Left Chief Councillor Heishilie Liangbi entered mourning; he was recalled from mourning and kept his former post.

translations.idiomatic: On renwu Deputy Commissioner for Military Affairs Yila Zijing was sent as birthday envoy to Song.

translations.literal: On gengyin, Section Vice Director Jiagu Alibu was made birthday envoy to Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Section Vice Director Jiagu Alibu was sent as birthday envoy to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，以大宗正丞糺為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on jiyou, Grand Imperial Clan Director Jiu was made birthday envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiyou, Grand Imperial Clan Director Jiu was sent as birthday envoy to Goryeo.

translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he went to Bazhou for the winter hunt.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上幸東宮。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.

translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Crown Prince Household Administrator Pucha Puyue and others were sent as envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.

translations.idiomatic: On guisi, because Western Xia had executed Ren Dejing, it sent envoys to offer thanks; an edict comforted and instructed them.

translations.idiomatic: Now I see what you memorialize—all according to regulations, with not one thing that benefits the state.

translations.idiomatic: If each day one thing were carried out, the yearly reckoning would show a surplus—how great the benefit would be!

translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, first month, on bingzi, the new moon, Song and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.

translations.idiomatic: On dingchou his sons Yong Sheng, Yong Dao, and Yongji were enfeoffed Prince of Xu, Prince of Teng, and Prince of Xue respectively.

translations.idiomatic: On renwu an edict ordered that officials who retired at seventy or above, regardless of rank, all received half salary.

translations.idiomatic: On bingshen orders were given to relieve the meng’an of Nanjing garrison fields stricken by flood.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “If the court’s own conduct is not upright, how can it set the empire right?

translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs receive many birthday and festival gifts—if these go uninvestigated while a minor official’s gift brings immediate impeachment, is that how to set the empire right?

sentences.zh: 癸亥，參知政事魏子平罷。

translations.literal: On guihai, Participation Councillor Wei Ziping was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Participation Councillor Wei Ziping was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高麗國王晛弟皓，廢其主自立，詐稱讓國，遣使以表來上。

translations.literal: Goryeo King Seon’s younger brother Hao deposed his lord and set himself up, falsely claiming to yield the state, and sent envoys with a memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo King Seon’s younger brother Hao deposed his lord and installed himself, falsely claiming to yield the state, and sent envoys with a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 五月辛卯，詔遣吏部侍郎靖使高麗問故。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on xinmao, an edict dispatched Vice Minister of Personnel Jing as envoy to Goryeo to inquire after the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinmao, an edict sent Vice Minister of Personnel Jing as envoy to Goryeo to inquire after the bereavement.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以南京留守移剌成為樞密副使。

translations.literal: On guisi, Nanjing military governor Yila Cheng was made vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Nanjing military governor Yila Cheng was appointed vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月己酉，詔曰：「諸路常貢數內，同州沙苑羊非急用，徒勞民爾，自今罷之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiyou, an edict said: “Among the regular tribute quotas of the circuits, the Shazhou sheep of Tong Prefecture are not urgently needed and only weary the people—forbear them from now on.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiyou, an edict said: “Among regular tribute quotas on the circuits, Shazhou sheep from Tong Prefecture are not urgently needed and only weary the people—abolish them from now on.

sentences.zh: 朕居深宮，勞民之事豈能盡知？

translations.literal: I dwell deep in the palace—how could I know all that wearies the people?
translations.idiomatic: I dwell deep in the palace—how could I know everything that wearies the people?

sentences.zh: 似此當具以聞。

translations.literal: Matters like this should be reported in full.”
translations.idiomatic: Matters like this should be reported in full.”

sentences.zh: 」戊午，觀稼於近郊。

translations.literal: ” On wuwu, he viewed the crops in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: ” On wuwu he viewed the crops in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 甲子，平章政事徒單合喜薨。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Chief Councillor Tushan Hexi died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Chief Councillor Tushan Hexi died.

sentences.zh: 七月甲申，參知政事宗敘薨。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on jiashen, Participation Councillor Zong Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jiashen, Participation Councillor Zong Xu died.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯朔，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on guimao, the new moon, the Great White star was seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao, the new moon, Venus shone by day.

sentences.zh: 詔朝臣曰：「朕嘗諭汝等，國家利便，治體遣闕，皆可直言。

translations.literal: An edict addressed the court ministers: “I have already told you that whatever serves the state’s advantage or reveals gaps in our governing institutions, you may speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: He addressed the court ministers: “I have told you before: whatever benefits the state, whatever gaps you see in how we govern—speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 外路官民亦嘗言事，汝等終無一語。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners on outer routes have also submitted memorials, yet you have not spoken a single word.
translations.idiomatic: People on the outer circuits have memorialized the throne, yet not one of you has said a word.

sentences.zh: 凡政事所行，豈能皆當？

translations.literal: How can every policy we enact be entirely right?
translations.idiomatic: Can everything we do in government be right?

sentences.zh: 自今直言得失，毋有所隱。

translations.literal: From now on speak plainly of gain and loss—hide nothing.”
translations.idiomatic: From now on speak plainly of success and failure—hide nothing.”

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，上謂宰臣曰：「隨朝之官，自謂曆一考則當得某職，兩考則當得某職。

translations.literal: On yisi, the emperor told the chief ministers: “Attendance officials suppose that after one tenure review they are due a certain post, and after two reviews another post.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he told the chief ministers: “Attendance officials think that after one review they are owed a certain post, after two reviews another.

sentences.zh: 第務因循，碌碌而已。

translations.literal: They only cultivate routine and remain mediocre.”
translations.idiomatic: They only go through the motions—mediocre drudges.”

sentences.zh: 自今以外路官與內除者，察其公勤則升用之，但苟簡於事，不須任滿，便以本品出之。

translations.literal: From now on, for outer-route officials and those appointed within, examine their public diligence and promote the diligent; if they are negligent in affairs, without waiting for their term to end send them out at their current rank.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for outer-route officials promoted within, weigh their diligence and promote the worthy; if they are slipshod in office, do not wait for their term to end—send them out at their present rank.

sentences.zh: 賞罰不明，豈能勸勉。

translations.literal: If rewards and punishments are unclear, how can we encourage effort?”
translations.idiomatic: If reward and punishment are unclear, how can you stir men to effort?”

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，詔曰：「應因窩斡被掠女直及諸色人未經刷放者，官為贖放。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict said: “All Jurchens and people of other categories captured during the Wohe troubles who have not yet been registered and released—the state shall ransom and release them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict ordered: “All Jurchens and people of other categories seized in the Wohe campaigns who have not yet been registered and released shall be ransomed and freed at government expense.

sentences.zh: 隱匿者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Whoever conceals them shall be punished under the statute on violating decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever hides them shall be charged with violating a decree.

sentences.zh: 其年幼不能稱說住貫者，從便住坐。

translations.literal: Those too young to state their place of registration may settle where convenient.”
translations.idiomatic: Children too young to name their registered domicile may settle where convenience allows.”

sentences.zh: 」上謂宰臣曰：「五品以下闕員甚多，而難於得人。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: “Below fifth rank there are many vacancies and yet men are hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: He told the chief ministers: “Below fifth rank the vacancies are many, yet good men are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 三品以上朕則知之，五品以下不能知也。

translations.literal: For third rank and above I know the men myself; for fifth rank and below I cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: I know the men of third rank and above myself; those of fifth rank and below I cannot know.

sentences.zh: 卿等會無一言見舉者。

translations.literal: You have never once put a name forward.
translations.idiomatic: You have never once recommended anyone to me.

sentences.zh: 欲畫久安之計，興百姓之利，而無良輔佐，所行皆尋常事耳，雖日日視朝，何益之有。

translations.literal: I wish to draw a plan for long peace and raise the people’s welfare, yet without good assistants everything done is ordinary business—what good is holding court day after day?
translations.idiomatic: I want a plan for lasting peace and the people’s welfare, but without able aides everything done is ordinary—and what good is holding court every day?

sentences.zh: 卿等宜勉思之。

translations.literal: You should strain to think on this.”
translations.idiomatic: Strain your minds over this.”

sentences.zh: 」己巳，以尚書刑部侍郎烏林答天錫等為賀宋生日使，近侍局使劉珫為夏國生日使。

translations.literal: On jisi, Vice Minister of Punishments Wulinada Tiansi and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the emperor’s birthday, and Palace Attendants Bureau Commissioner Liu Ku envoy to congratulate Western Xia on the emperor’s birthday.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Vice Minister of Punishments Wulinada Tiansi and others were sent as birthday envoys to Song, and Palace Attendants Bureau Commissioner Liu Ku as birthday envoy to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 九月癸未，獵於橫山。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on guiwei, hunt at Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei, he hunted at Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，還都。

translations.literal: On gengyin, returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月壬寅朔，以左宣徽使敬嗣暉為參知政事。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on renyin, the new moon, Left Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Services Jing Sihui was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on renyin, the new moon, Left Bureau of Palace Services Commissioner Jing Sihui was appointed participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上謂宰臣曰：「朕已行之事，卿等以為成命不可複更，但承順而已，一無執奏。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the emperor told the chief ministers: “For matters I have already carried out, you think the settled decree cannot be changed again and only comply—you never once memorialize in dissent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he told the chief ministers: “For what I have already done, you treat the decree as fixed and only obey—you never once argue back.

sentences.zh: 且卿等凡有奏，何嘗不從。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever you submit a memorial, when have I not followed it?
translations.idiomatic: When have I ever refused a memorial of yours?

sentences.zh: 自今朕旨雖出，宜審而行，有未便者，即奏改之。

translations.literal: From now on, though my orders go forth, you should examine them in execution; where something is unsuitable, memorialize at once to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, though my orders go out, weigh them as you carry them out; if anything is wrong, memorialize and have it changed.

sentences.zh: 或在下位有言尚書省所行未便，亦當從而改之，毋拒而不從。

translations.literal: If someone in a lower post says that what the Secretariat has done is unsuitable, you should likewise revise it—do not refuse and ignore him.”
translations.idiomatic: If men below say the Secretariat’s acts are wrong, change them too—do not refuse and shut them out.”

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，尚書左丞相紇石烈良弼進《睿宗實錄》。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Left Chief Councillor Hesheli Liangbi presented the Veritable Records of Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Left Chief Councillor Hesheli Liangbi presented the Veritable Records of Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，上謂宰臣曰：「衍慶宮圖畫功臣，已命增為二十人。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the emperor told the chief ministers: “Portraits of meritorious ministers in Yanqing Palace—I have ordered the number increased to twenty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he told the chief ministers: “The portrait gallery of merit at Yanqing Palace—I have ordered it raised to twenty men.

sentences.zh: 如丞相韓企先，自本朝興國以來，憲章法度，多出其手。

translations.literal: Minister Han Qixian, since our dynasty rose to power, has had statutes and institutions largely from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Take Chancellor Han Qixian: since our state rose, statutes and institutions have largely come from his hand.

sentences.zh: 至於關決大政，但與大臣謀議，終不使外人知覺。

translations.literal: On deciding great affairs, he discusses only with chief ministers and never lets outsiders know.
translations.idiomatic: On settling great affairs he counsels only with senior ministers and never lets outsiders know.

sentences.zh: 漢人宰相，前後無比，若褒顯之，亦足示勸，慎無遺之。」

translations.literal: Among Han chief ministers, none before or after compare; to honor him would suffice as encouragement—be careful not to omit him.”
translations.idiomatic: No Han chancellor before or after compares; to honor him would teach later men—see that he is not left out.”

sentences.zh: 十一月丁丑，以西南路招討使宗甯等為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on dingchou, Southwest Route Pacification Commissioner Zong Ning and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingchou, Southwest Route Pacification Commissioner Zong Ning and others were sent as New Year envoys to Song.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，幸東宮。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he visited the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上謂皇太子曰：「吾兒在儲貳之位，朕為汝措天下，當無複有經營之事。

translations.literal: The emperor told the heir apparent: “My son, in the position of heir designate, I have set the realm in order for you—there ought to be no further labor of founding.
translations.idiomatic: He told the crown prince: “Son, as heir I have arranged the realm for you—you ought not need to build it anew.

sentences.zh: 汝惟無忘祖宗純厚之風，以勤修道德為孝，明信賞罰為治而已。

translations.literal: You need only never forget the pure and generous customs of our ancestors, take diligent cultivation of virtue as filial piety, and clear reward and punishment as governance.”
translations.idiomatic: Only never forget our ancestors’ plain and generous ways; make diligent virtue your filial duty and clear reward and punishment your rule.”

sentences.zh: 昔唐太宗謂其子高宗曰：'吾伐高麗不克終，汝可繼之。

translations.literal: In old times Emperor Taizong of Tang told his son Emperor Gaozong: “I could not finish conquering Goryeo; you may continue it.”
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Tang Taizong told his son Gaozong: “I could not finish conquering Goryeo—you may take it up.”

sentences.zh: '如此之事，朕不以遺汝。

translations.literal: “Matters like this I do not bequeath to you.”
translations.idiomatic: “Matters like that I do not leave to you.”

sentences.zh: 如遼之海濱王，以國人愛其子，嫉而殺之，此何理也。

translations.literal: Like Liao’s Prince of the Coast—because the people loved his son, he grew jealous and killed him; what principle is this?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Liao’s Prince of the Coast—because the people loved his son, he grew jealous and killed him. What principle is that?

sentences.zh: 子為眾愛，愈為美事，所為若此，安有不亡。

translations.literal: For a son to be loved by the masses is all the more a fine thing; conduct such as that—how could ruin not follow?
translations.idiomatic: For a son to be loved by the people is the finer thing; act as he did—how could the state not perish?

sentences.zh: 唐太宗有道之君，而謂其子高宗曰：'爾于李績無恩。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was a ruler of the Way, yet he told his son Emperor Gaozong: “You owe Li Ji no favor.”
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was a ruler of the Way, yet he told Gaozong: “You owe Li Ji no debt of grace.”

sentences.zh: 今以事出之，我死，宜即授以僕射，彼必致死力矣。

translations.literal: “Now I am sending him out on duty; when I die, you should at once appoint him Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—then he will surely exert himself unto death.”
translations.idiomatic: “Now I am sending him away on business; when I die, make him Vice Director at once—then he will give his life in service.”

sentences.zh: '君人者，焉用偽為。

translations.literal: “What need has a ruler for pretense?”
translations.idiomatic: “What need has a ruler for pretense?”

sentences.zh: 受恩于父，安有忘報於子者乎？

translations.literal: One who received grace from the father—how could he forget to repay the son?
translations.idiomatic: Men who owe a father grace—how could they forget to repay the son?

sentences.zh: 朕禦臣下，惟以誠實耳。

translations.literal: I govern my ministers only with sincerity.”
translations.idiomatic: I govern my ministers only with sincerity.”

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The officials all cried “Long life!”
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers all cried “Long life!”

sentences.zh: 丙戌，朝享於太廟。

translations.literal: On bingxu, morning audience and offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he offered morning sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，有事於圓丘，大赦。

translations.literal: On dinghai, performed rites at the Circular Mound Altar; great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he sacrificed at the Circular Mound Altar and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，群臣奉上尊號曰應天興祚欽文廣武仁德聖孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On guisi, the ministers offered the honorific Responding to Heaven, Raising the Fate, Esteeming Culture, Magnifying Martiality, Benevolent Virtue, Sacredly Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the ministers offered the style Responding to Heaven and Raising the Fate, Esteeming Culture and Magnifying Martiality, Benevolent Virtue and Sacred Filiality Emperor.

sentences.zh: 乙未，詔中外。

translations.literal: On yiwei, an edict to the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei an edict was issued to court and realm.
